South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 09/15/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD exacerbation management, evaluation of renal function, and reassessment of mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up two weeks after initiating treatment for his COPD exacerbation. He reports slight improvement in his respiratory symptoms since starting oral prednisone, noting decreased frequency of nighttime awakenings and a reduction in the use of his albuterol inhaler to three times daily. However, he continues to experience dyspnea during exertion and a persistent cough with minimal sputum production. He expresses concern regarding the ongoing shortness of breath, particularly when climbing stairs.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant issue. Mr. Fairfax describes the swelling as persistent, with minimal improvement despite adherence to dietary sodium restrictions and diuretic therapy. He reports increased discomfort, rating it as a 7/10, particularly after prolonged periods of sitting. He has been diligently monitoring his weight, noting a slight increase which raises concern for potential fluid retention.
In terms of mental health, Mr. Fairfax acknowledges some improvement in his mood since the last visit, attributing this to increased social interaction with neighbors. However, he still experiences episodes of anxiety, particularly related to his health status, and continues to have difficulties with insomnia.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + mild dyspnea, + cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using three times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 160 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 78, BP 130/84, RR 22, O2 sat 80% on room air.
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but more engaged than previous visit. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.2, Hgb 10.0, Hct 30.0, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.5, Cl 96, CO2 25, BUN 40, Cr 2.5, Glucose 92. 3. BNP: 680 (decreased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.7 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax shows slight improvement in respiratory symptoms; however, he remains symptomatic. Continue current inhaler regimen. A follow-up pulmonary function test is scheduled for next month to evaluate lung function post-exacerbation. Consideration for a referral to pulmonary rehabilitation to enhance his exercise tolerance and improve overall quality of life. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Monitor renal function closely given the recent improvement in serum creatinine. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists, with a slight increase in weight noted. A referral to nephrology will be pursued for further evaluation and optimization of diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage daily weight monitoring. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A follow-up with psychiatry is scheduled in one week for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Explore additional therapeutic options such as cognitive-behavioral therapy to address anxiety and insomnia.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
